audience: Accountants who record newly purchased factory machinery as a fixed asset and want to check how it affects the books.
goal: Create a **fixed asset** for new factory equipment from the **Factory Equipments** asset model, **Confirm** it so it becomes **Running**, then prove the result in two reports: the **Trial Balance** and the **General Ledger** (with draft entries included).
before: You can open the **Accounting** app and its **Accounting** menu (the Assets screen).
An asset model called **Factory Equipments** exists. It supplies the 72-month duration and the three accounts: Fixed Asset **11010170**, Depreciation **11020170** and Expense **72090050**.
You know the purchase cost. This guide uses **100,000**.
outcome: A new asset exists with status **Running** and an original value of 100,000.
The Trial Balance and General Ledger show the scheduled **depreciation entry** for the asset, as a draft entry.
You know how to see draft (not yet posted) entries in a report.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**. The asset name carries a `[TEST]` tag and a random code so every run creates a new, uniquely named asset.
The depreciation entry is **scheduled**, not posted: it stays a draft until its date. That is why the reports need **Include Draft Entries** switched on.

The depreciation amount in the screenshots (729.93) is only part of a month, because the asset was acquired mid-month and depreciation is **based on days per period**. Your figure depends on your acquisition date.
In the General Ledger screenshots you may see a second, similar line. It comes from an earlier test run that created another asset; only the line carrying **your** asset name is yours.
Each test run leaves a confirmed asset behind. Cancel or archive test assets on the test database when you no longer need them.

phases.title: Open the Assets screen
phases.summary: Go from the Accounting app to the list of fixed assets.
phases.checkpoint: The **Assets** list is open, with a **New** button at the top left.

phases.title: Create and confirm the asset
phases.summary: Name the asset, pick the model, enter the cost and confirm.
phases.checkpoint: The asset is **Running**, with a book value of **100,000**.

phases.title: Check the Trial Balance
phases.summary: Open the Trial Balance with draft entries included and find the depreciation accounts.
phases.checkpoint: The Trial Balance lists the **Depreciation Expense** and **Provision for Depreciation** accounts with the scheduled amount.

phases.title: Check the General Ledger
phases.summary: Open the General Ledger and find the draft depreciation line for your asset.
phases.checkpoint: The General Ledger shows the draft depreciation line named after your asset.

glossary.meaning: Something the company owns and uses for years, such as a machine. Its cost is spread over its useful life instead of being expensed at once.
A template that pre-fills the depreciation method, duration and accounts, so every asset of the same kind is set up the same way.
What the asset cost to acquire.
The share of the asset's cost charged to expense each period. Here it runs over 72 months.
The balance-sheet account that collects depreciation charged so far (11020170).
A journal entry that is scheduled but **not posted** yet. It does not count in reports unless you switch on **Include Draft Entries**.
A report listing every account with its debit and credit totals.
A report listing every account with the individual journal lines behind its balance.

1.title: Open the Accounting app
1.do: On the Odoo home screen, click the **Accounting** app.
actions: Go to the Odoo home screen.
Find the **Accounting** icon.
Click it.
1.see: The Accounting app opens with its menu bar across the top.
1.why: Fixed assets are managed inside the Accounting app.

2.title: Open the Accounting menu
2.do: In the top menu bar, click **Accounting**.
actions: Look at the menu bar across the top.
Click **Accounting** (not the app icon).
2.see: A drop-down with the Accounting entries, including **Assets**.
2.why: The Assets screen sits in this drop-down, under the Management group.
2.tip: If you cannot see the menu, widen the browser window; narrow windows hide the last entries behind a **+**.

3.title: Open Assets
actions: Find **Assets** in the Management group.
Click it.
Wait for the list to load.
3.see: The **Assets** list showing every existing asset with its model, acquisition date, values and status.
3.why: This list is where every fixed asset is created and followed.

4.title: Start a new asset
4.do: Click the purple **New** button at the top left.
actions: Find the **New** button next to the title **Assets**.
Click it.
4.see: An empty asset form with status **Draft**.
4.why: A new asset starts as a Draft. Nothing is posted to the books until you confirm it.

5.title: Enter the asset name
5.do: Type a name for the asset in the **Asset Name** field.
actions: Click the large **Asset Name** field at the top of the form.
Type the name, for example **Factory Equipment - New Machine**.
5.see: Your name appears in large letters at the top of the form.
5.why: The name identifies the asset everywhere, and it is copied into the depreciation entries you check at the end.
5.tip: Use a name that says what and which one it is, so you can find its depreciation lines later.

6.title: Select the asset model
actions: Click the **Asset Model** field.
Type **Factory Equipments**.
Click **FACTORY EQUIPMENTS** in the list.
6.see: The form fills in by itself: **Duration 72 Months**, Fixed Asset Account **11010170**, Depreciation Account **11020170** and Expense Account **72090050**.
6.why: The model supplies the depreciation settings and accounts, so you do not have to enter them for each machine.
6.warning: Check the three account codes after choosing the model. Wrong accounts mean the depreciation posts to the wrong place.

7.title: Enter the original value
actions: Click the **Original Value** field.
Press **Tab** to confirm the number.
7.see: The field shows 100,000 and **Book Value** on the right follows it.
7.why: The original value is the acquisition cost. Depreciation is calculated from it over the 72 months.
7.tip: Enter the cost without the currency symbol or thousands separators.

8.title: Confirm the asset
8.do: Click **Confirm** at the top left of the form.
actions: Find the **Confirm** button above the form.
Click it.
Watch the status bar change.
8.see: The status changes from **Draft** to **Running**. **Depreciation Board** appears as a tab, and the chatter logs *Asset created*.
8.why: Confirming starts the depreciation. Odoo creates the schedule of monthly depreciation entries, all as drafts until their date.
8.warning: A running asset cannot simply be edited. To change it later you use **Modify Depreciation**.

9.title: Find the Reporting menu
9.do: Look at the top menu bar and find **Reporting**.
actions: Look along the top menu bar.
If **Reporting** is hidden, click the **+** at the end of the bar to reveal it.
9.see: The **Reporting** menu is available (directly, or behind the **+**).
9.why: The reports you need next live under Reporting.

10.title: Open the Trial Balance
actions: Open the **Reporting** menu.
Click **Trial Balance**.
Wait for the report to load.
10.see: The **Trial Balance**, listing every account with Initial Balance, current period and End Balance columns.
10.why: The Trial Balance shows whether the new asset and its depreciation reached the right accounts.

11.title: Open the report options
11.do: Click the **Options** button at the top of the report.
actions: Find **Options** in the row of filters.
Click it.
11.see: A small menu with report options, including **Include Draft Entries**.
11.why: By default a report counts only **posted** entries. The depreciation is still a draft, so you need an option to show it.

12.title: Include draft entries
12.where: Trial Balance > Options > Include Draft Entries
actions: Click **Include Draft Entries** in the menu.
Wait for the report to reload.
12.see: The button now reads **Options: With Draft Entries** and the report reloads with the scheduled depreciation included.
12.why: The first monthly depreciation entry is scheduled to post automatically at month end. Including drafts lets you see it now.

13.title: Check the depreciation accounts
13.do: Find the **72090050 Depreciation** and **11020170 Provision for Depreciation** accounts.
actions: Scroll down the list of accounts.
Find **11020170 PROVISION FOR DEPRECIATION - FACTORY EQUIPMENT** (outlined in red).
Read its credit in the current-period column, then find **72090050** the same way.
points: Both show the same scheduled amount for the period.
13.see: Both accounts show the scheduled depreciation for the new asset in the current period.
13.why: Equal debit and credit on these two accounts confirms the asset is depreciating into the accounts the model set.
13.tip: The Fixed Asset account 11010170 appears too. Its balance only moves once the acquisition entry is posted.

14.title: Find the Reporting menu again
14.do: Look at the top menu bar again and find **Reporting**.
actions: Look along the top menu bar.
If **Reporting** is hidden again, click the **+** at the end of the bar.
14.why: The menu closes after each navigation, so you open it again for the next report.

15.title: Open the General Ledger
15.where: Accounting app > Reporting > Audit Reports > General Ledger
actions: Open the **Reporting** menu.
In the **Audit Reports** group, click **General Ledger**.
Wait for the report to load.
15.see: The **General Ledger**, listing every account with its totals.
15.why: Where the Trial Balance gives totals, the General Ledger shows the individual journal lines behind them.

16.title: Open the report options
16.do: Click the **Options** button at the top of the report.
actions: Find **Options** in the row of filters.
Click it.
16.see: The options menu with **Include Draft Entries**.
16.why: Filters reset for each report, so draft entries must be switched on again.

17.title: Include draft entries
17.where: General Ledger > Options > Include Draft Entries
actions: Click **Include Draft Entries**.
Wait for the report to reload.
17.see: The button reads **Options: With Draft Entries**.
17.why: Without this, the draft depreciation line for the new asset would not appear.

18.title: Expand the depreciation expense account
actions: Find the row for account **72090050**.
Click its name.
The journal lines under it appear.
18.see: The account unfolds to show each journal line with its date, communication and amount.
18.why: Expanding an account is how you reach the individual entries behind its balance.

19.title: Check the depreciation entry
19.do: Find the line named after your asset, ending in **: Depreciation**.
actions: Look through the lines under account 72090050.
Find the line that starts with your asset name (outlined in red).
Check its date and amount.
points: The line is dated at **month end**.
Its amount is the depreciation for the part of the month the asset was in use.
It is a **draft** entry until its date, when it posts automatically.
19.see: A draft depreciation line named after your asset, with its scheduled date and amount.
19.why: This is the end result of the tour: the asset you created has produced its first scheduled depreciation entry in the right account.
19.tip: That completes the tour: create the asset, confirm it, and verify the depreciation in the Trial Balance and General Ledger.
